comparison: Perfect agreement on C115. Both evaluations support the validation of the random walk model using Wright-Fisher simulations. OpenEval notes empirical agreement with caveats about regime validity; peer review implicitly accepts this through endorsement of coalescent time predictions.

Strong agreement on C82, C87, C88, C90 regarding the expiring fitness model. Both evaluations support the model's validity and analysis. OpenEval emphasizes clear definition and acknowledged limitations; peer review explicitly praises the analysis and notes important additions substantiating the SIR connection.

Strong agreement on C48, C57, C58, C61, C62 regarding partial sweeps as core finding. Both evaluations support this central result. OpenEval emphasizes Figure 1 demonstration of distinction between homogeneous and heterogeneous dynamics; peer review provides explicit affirmation from all three reviewers and editor.

Agreement on C5, C130, C131 regarding reconciliation of adaptive evolution with quasi-neutral dynamics. Both evaluations support this synthesis. OpenEval finds it well-supported by model and empirical observations; peer review explicitly endorses the reconciliation as interesting and explanatory.

Agreement on C136, C139 regarding generalization to broader eco-evolutionary contexts. Both evaluations support this extension. OpenEval notes logical reasoning with caveat about needing empirical validation in other systems; peer review endorses potential universality beyond human RNA viruses.

Disagreement on C11, C12, C13 regarding critique of traveling wave framework. OpenEval supports the critical assessment as well-justified; peer review rates as uncertain, with Reviewer 1 challenging that the characterization of existing methods may be overstated and that the distinction 'remains blurred.'

Agreement on C94, C97, C123 regarding influenza empirical observations. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes clear demonstration with caveat about retrospective nature; peer review confirms observation while noting temporal limitations (2013-2020 period).

Agreement on C127, C128, C129 regarding parameter-dependent conditions for sweep completeness. Both evaluations support this dichotomy. OpenEval notes derivation from model; peer review explicitly accepts the distinction between homogeneous and immunologically diverse populations.

Agreement on C19, C20 regarding connections to ecological theory. Both evaluations support this conceptual link. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and clear framing; peer review explicitly endorses placement into broader context of consumer resource dynamics.

Agreement on C66, C67 regarding ecological model comparisons. Both evaluations support these connections. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations; peer review endorses the qualitative connection offering additional intuition for host-pathogen interactions.

Agreement on C99, C100, C124 regarding SARS-CoV-2 dynamics. Both evaluations support these observations. OpenEval notes clear demonstration with caveat about retrospective analysis; peer review accepts characterization of SARS-CoV-2 as more predictable than influenza without challenge.

Significant disagreement on C102 and related unpredictability claims (C4, C21, C22 in peer R2). OpenEval supports the random walk abstraction and zero-mean property; peer review rates as uncertain, with Reviewer 1 stating the unpredictability claim 'remains somewhat misleading' and challenging that quasi-neutrality does not imply full stochasticity.

Partial overlap on C18 regarding model behaviors. OpenEval supports summary of key behaviors from simulations; peer review focuses on C3 and partial sweep findings (C48, C57, C58, C61, C62) with strong support, implicitly accepting C18 as part of core finding.
OpenEval supports C1, C6, C120, C121 as well-documented background on RNA virus evolution. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.
OpenEval supports C14, C15, C28, C31, C32, C33 describing model structure and assumptions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these model construction claims.
OpenEval supports C50, C51, C52, C54, C56 explaining why heterogeneous immunity is necessary for realistic dynamics. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these mechanistic explanations.

OpenEval supports C24, C25, C92, C93, C122, C123 regarding prediction problem and empirical motivation. While C123 appears in peer R6, the full set of prediction difficulty claims is not directly evaluated by peer review.
OpenEval supports C140, C141 describing data sources and methods. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological claims.

OpenEval rates C36, C63, C118, C119 as uncertain, noting they are largely speculative or provide general context without direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these claims.
